Introduction","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":40,"modality":0,"text":"HTTP semantics ([HTTP]) are used for a broad range ofservices on the Internet. These semantics","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":41,"modality":0,"text":"have most commonly been used with HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2. HTTP/1.1 has been used over a variety","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":42,"modality":0,"text":"oftransport and session layers, while HTTP/2 has been used primarily with TLS over TCP. HTTP/3","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":43,"modality":0,"text":"supports the same semantics over a new transport protocol: QUIC.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":44,"modality":0,"text":"1.1. Prior Versions of HTTP","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":45,"modality":0,"text":"HTTP/1.1 ([HTTP/1.1]) uses whitespace-delimited text ﬁelds to convey HTTP messages. While these","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":46,"modality":0,"text":"exchanges are human readable, using whitespace for message formatting leads to parsing","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":47,"modality":0,"text":"complexity and excessive tolerance ofvariant behavior.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":48,"modality":0,"text":"Because HTTP/1.1 does not include a multiplexing layer, multiple TCP connections are often used","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":49,"modality":0,"text":"to service requests in parallel. However, that has a negative impact on congestion control and","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":50,"modality":0,"text":"network eﬃciency, since TCP does not share congestion control across multiple connections.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":51,"modality":0,"text":"HTTP/2 ([HTTP/2]) introduced a binary framing and multiplexing layer to improve latency","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":52,"modality":0,"text":"without modifying the transport layer. However, because the parallel nature ofHTTP/2's","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":53,"modality":0,"text":"multiplexing is not visible to TCP's loss recovery mechanisms, a lost or reordered packet causes","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":54,"modality":0,"text":"all active transactions to experience a stall regardless ofwhether that transaction was directly","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":55,"modality":0,"text":"impacted by the lost packet.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":56,"modality":0,"text":"1.2. Delegation to QUIC","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":57,"modality":0,"text":"The QUIC transport protocol incorporates stream multiplexing and per-stream ﬂow control,","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":58,"modality":0,"text":"similar to that provided by the HTTP/2 framing layer. By providing reliability at the stream level","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":59,"modality":0,"text":"and congestion control across the entire connection, QUIC has the capability to improve the","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":60,"modality":0,"text":"performance ofHTTP compared to a TCP mapping. QUIC also incorporates TLS 1.3 ([TLS]) at the","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":61,"modality":0,"text":"transport layer, oﬀering comparable conﬁdentiality and integrity to running TLS over TCP, with","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":62,"modality":0,"text":"the improved connection setup latency ofTCP Fast Open ([TFO]).","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":63,"modality":0,"text":"This document deﬁnes HTTP/3: a mapping ofHTTP semantics over the QUIC transport protocol,","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":64,"modality":0,"text":"drawing heavily on the design ofHTTP/2. HTTP/3 relies on QUIC to provide conﬁdentiality and","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":65,"modality":0,"text":"integrity protection of data; peer authentication; and reliable, in-order, per-stream delivery.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":66,"modality":0,"text":"While delegating stream lifetime and ﬂow-control issues to QUIC, a binary framing similar to the","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":67,"modality":0,"text":"HTTP/2 framing is used on each stream. Some HTTP/2 features are subsumed by QUIC, while other","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":68,"modality":0,"text":"features are implemented atop QUIC.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":69,"modality":0,"text":"QUIC is described in [QUIC-TRANSPORT]. For a full description ofHTTP/2, see [HTTP/2].","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":70,"modality":0,"text":"Bishop Standards Track Page 5","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":71,"modality":0,"text":"RFC 9114 HTTP/3 June 2022","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":72,"modality":0,"text":"2. HTTP/3 Protocol Overview","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":73,"modality":0,"text":"HTTP/3 provides a transport for HTTP semantics using the QUIC transport protocol and an","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":74,"modality":0,"text":"internal framing layer similar to HTTP/2.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":75,"modality":0,"text":"Once a client knows that an HTTP/3 server exists at a certain endpoint, it opens a QUIC","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":76,"modality":0,"text":"connection. QUIC provides protocol negotiation, stream-based multiplexing, and ﬂow control.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":77,"modality":0,"text":"Discovery of an HTTP/3 endpoint is described in Section 3.1.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":78,"modality":0,"text":"Within each stream, the basic unit ofHTTP/3 communication is a frame (Section 7.2). Each frame","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":79,"modality":0,"text":"type serves a diﬀerent purpose. For example, HEADERS and DATA frames form the basis ofHTTP","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":80,"modality":0,"text":"requests and responses (Section 4.1). Frames that apply to the entire connection are conveyed on","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":81,"modality":0,"text":"a dedicated control stream.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":82,"modality":0,"text":"Multiplexing ofrequests is performed using the QUIC stream abstraction, which is described in","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":83,"modality":0,"text":"Section 2 of [QUIC-TRANSPORT]. Each request-response pair consumes a single QUIC stream.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":84,"modality":0,"text":"Streams are independent of each other, so one stream that is blocked or suﬀers packet loss does","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":85,"modality":0,"text":"not prevent progress on other streams.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":86,"modality":0,"text":"Server push is an interaction mode introduced in HTTP/2 ([HTTP/2]) that permits a server to push","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":87,"modality":0,"text":"a request-response exchange to a client in anticipation ofthe client making the indicated request.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":88,"modality":0,"text":"This trades oﬀnetwork usage against a potential latency gain. Several HTTP/3 frames are used to","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":89,"modality":0,"text":"manage server push, such as PUSH_PROMISE, MAX_PUSH_ID, and CANCEL_PUSH.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":90,"modality":0,"text":"As in HTTP/2, request and response ﬁelds are compressed for transmission. Because HPACK","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":91,"modality":0,"text":"([HPACK]) relies on in-order transmission of compressed ﬁeld sections (a guarantee not provided","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":92,"modality":0,"text":"by QUIC), HTTP/3 replaces HPACKwith QPACK ([QPACK]). Cross-Protocol Attacks","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"contextIndex":8,"modality":0,"text":"The following sections provide a detailed overview ofthe lifecycle of an HTTP/3 connection:","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"contextIndex":9,"modality":0,"text":"• "Connection Setup and Management" (Section 3) covers how an HTTP/3 endpoint is","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"contextIndex":10,"modality":0,"text":"discovered and an HTTP/3 connection is established.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"contextIndex":11,"modality":0,"text":"• "Expressing HTTP Semantics in HTTP/3" (Section 4) describes how HTTP semantics are","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"contextIndex":12,"modality":0,"text":"expressed using frames.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"contextIndex":13,"modality":0,"text":"• "Connection Closure" (Section 5) describes how HTTP/3 connections are terminated, either","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"contextIndex":14,"modality":0,"text":"gracefully or abruptly.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"contextIndex":15,"modality":0,"text":"The details ofthe wire protocol and interactions with the transport are described in subsequent","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}}],"openOrConflictedClaims":[],"retrievedEvidence":[],"layoutEvidence":[],"visualEvidence":[]}}
